p01_17.header_year: The filename year (2022-2023) is CORRECT and matches the actual reported data. Evidence: (1) page 1's own running header reads 'Common Data Set 2022-2023', matching the filename, and is the header for the general-information/respondent section that would be filled in last/checked most carefully. (2) B1 enrollment counts are explicitly dated 'as of the institution's official fall reporting date or as of October 19, 2022' (page 3) — that is Fall 2022 data, i.e., a 2022-2023-cycle CDS. (3) C1/C9/F1 admissions and enrollment data are explicitly for 'Fall 2022' applicants/enrollees (pages 7, 9, 10, 16). (4) Page 4's graduation-rate instructions cite 'the IPEDS GRS Forms and Instructions for the 2022-2023 Survey.' (5) Section G (page 17) asks for '2023-2024 academic year' costs of attendance, which is exactly the forward-looking cost data a 2022-2023 CDS collects (CDS G-section costs are always for the upcoming academic year relative to the CDS cycle). CONCLUSION: pages 3 through 17 all carry a STALE, INCORRECT running header that says 'Common Data Set 2021-2022' — almost certainly because Cornell copied last year's template pages for sections B onward and never updated the running header text, while pages 1-2 (the A section, edited separately/more recently) got the correct header. Any page-routing or citation logic that trusts the per-page header string for pages 3-17 will mislabel the survey year; the header string must be ignored in favor of the filename/cover-page year for this document.
p01_17.c7_marker_semantics: Verified directly from the page 8 image. The mark is a plain typed capital 'X' (no checkmark glyph, no filled/shaded box — cells are open rectangles from a bordered table, and Cornell typed an 'X' character into exactly one cell per row). CRITICALLY: the mark itself carries NO information — every X on the page is visually identical. The meaning is carried ENTIRELY by which of the four columns (Very Important | Important | Considered | Not Considered) the X's cell falls under. Confirmed examples from the image: 'Rigor of secondary school record' -> X under Very Important; 'Class rank' -> X under Important (a different column than the row above it); 'Standardized test scores' -> X under Considered; 'Religious affiliation/commitment' -> X under Not Considered; 'Level of applicant's interest' -> X under Not Considered. The bare text layer (pymupdf get_text()) emits these as a flat sequence of row-label-then-'X' pairs with the four column header strings extracted separately at the top of the block and NO x/y-coordinate or column association carried through in plain reading order. THEREFORE: the text layer is UNUSABLE for recovering C7 (and by extension any same-shaped grid, see layout_warnings) — this grid must be read either from (a) word-level bounding-box coordinates (get_text('words') or get_text('dict') with column x-ranges) or (b) the rendered image, not from plain top-to-bottom/reading-order text extraction.
